hyperedges.label: Physics bridge with authority declared by body type
Single ordering authority: lanes → stages → constraints
Collider → filtered contact → script callback chain

nodes.label: AtlasJS Engine
nodes.rationale: Modern 2D-first TypeScript game engine designed as a plugin ecosystem so every major system can evolve independently while staying cohesive.

nodes.label: Performance Principle
nodes.rationale: Performance is considered from the start: abstractions must improve architecture without hiding runtime costs; avoid unnecessary allocations and abstraction overhead.

nodes.label: Modularity Principle
nodes.rationale: Each major system has one focused responsibility isolated in an independent package, so AtlasJS behaves as an ecosystem of composable modules rather than a monolith.

nodes.label: Plugin-based Architecture
nodes.rationale: The core stays lightweight and independent from optional systems; rendering, physics, ECS and tooling integrate through well-defined extension points so new capabilities never require core edits.

nodes.label: Extensibility Principle
nodes.rationale: Decisions favor long-term flexibility and clear extension points over short-term convenience, so implementations can be replaced or experimented with.

nodes.label: packages/ — Reusable Engine Modules
nodes.rationale: Packages must stay focused and independent and may never depend on an application in apps/, keeping the dependency direction one-way.

nodes.label: apps/ — Executable Applications
nodes.rationale: Applications compose packages, but application-specific logic must not leak back into reusable engine packages.

nodes.label: AI Agent Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Architecture consistency is explicitly ranked above the quickest possible solution; always type code, avoid comments, avoid circular dependencies, prefer extending existing systems.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Codebase questions go through `graphify query` first because a scoped subgraph is much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

nodes.label: 2D-first, 3D-ready Architectural Direction
nodes.rationale: Focus is 2D today, but no decision may make future 3D evolution impossible without a strong reason; foundational APIs avoid 2D-only assumptions.

nodes.label: Turborepo Starter Template
nodes.rationale: Unmodified upstream create-turbo boilerplate; describes docs/web/@repo/ui packages that do not exist in this repo, so it is stale relative to CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: React + TypeScript + Vite Template
nodes.rationale: Unmodified Vite React-TS scaffold README; documents ESLint/react-compiler options rather than the dino-brawl game itself.

nodes.label: Dino Brawl HTML Entry Point
nodes.rationale: Mounts the React shell at #root via /src/main.tsx; the <title> was renamed to "Dino Brawl" as part of the sandbox → dino-brawl rename.

nodes.label: WebGPU Demo HTML Entry Point
nodes.rationale: Non-React demo: a bare #webgpu-canvas driven by /src/index.ts, used to exercise nebula scene-graph primitives directly.

nodes.label: Asset (serializable descriptor)
nodes.rationale: An asset is a behaviour-free POJO ({type,id}) describing WHAT to load; dispose() was removed from it because lifetime belongs only to the live resource.

nodes.label: Resource (runtime handle)
nodes.rationale: The loaded, non-serializable handle owning destroy(); named Resource and using destroy() (not dispose) to align with nebula's Disposable without importing it.

nodes.label: AssetLoader<A, R>
nodes.rationale: One loader per asset `type`, registered by the owning domain plugin — the only place that knows HOW to load, keeping the manager backend-agnostic.

nodes.label: LoadContext
nodes.rationale: Deliberately minimal seam passed to loaders so dependency loads go back through the same manager (and thus the same cache/dedup); left open for progress/cancel later.

nodes.label: AssetManager
nodes.rationale: Orchestrator (register/load/get/destroy) implementing LoadContext itself; keeps loaded resources and destroys them all at teardown — no refcount in v1.

nodes.label: TextureAsset
nodes.rationale: Lives in @atlasjs/nebula, not in @atlasjs/assets, so the assets package stays a 100% generic leaf with no backend knowledge.

nodes.label: TextureLoader
nodes.rationale: Encapsulates the DOM path (Image → decode → createImageBitmap flipY → createTexture2D) that dino-brawl's EcsScene.loadTexture used to do by hand.

nodes.label: SpriteLoader
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates composition: it calls ctx.load(asset.texture) so a shared texture across N sprites yields exactly one GPU Texture2D.

nodes.label: Sprite (gameplay resource handle)
nodes.rationale: Moved from `implements Asset` to `implements Resource` with a no-op destroy() because it does not own its texture; `kind` dropped since the discriminant lives on the descriptor.

nodes.label: *Node scene-graph naming convention
nodes.rationale: Renaming nebula Sprite/Shape/Rect/Circle/Line to *Node kills the Sprite(node) ↔ Sprite(asset) collision at the source (no more import aliasing), self-documents the scene graph, and matches what the editor already expects.

nodes.label: Load deduplication by asset id
nodes.rationale: The Promise (not the resolved value) is cached, so concurrent loads of the same id collapse into one; cache key is id-only, safe today only because ids are prefixed `texture:`/`sprite:`.

nodes.label: Dependency reference by value
nodes.rationale: v1 composes descriptors (SpriteAsset holds a TextureAsset) instead of referencing by id; AssetRef-by-id is deferred to the compiler/editor era, which is also what blocks scene serialization.

nodes.label: NebulaPlugin → AssetPlugin coupling
nodes.rationale: Accepted cost of declared plugin deps (there is no optional `requires`): Nebula can no longer boot without the asset system. A dedicated bridge plugin was rejected as over-engineering while there is one loader per domain.

nodes.label: AtlasJS Unified Backlog
nodes.rationale: Single list of everything not yet done, grouped by domain, each item pointing back to its source design doc; statuses are 📋 not implemented / 🔶 partial / 💭 vision.

nodes.label: A2 — Text rendering
nodes.rationale: Bitmap/MSDF font as a built-in "text" shader plus glyph batch, plugging in as a Batcher on the NodeRenderer seam (E3).

nodes.label: A3 — Post-processing stack
nodes.rationale: Chained passes (bloom, vignette) on an offscreen RenderTarget; the render-to-texture hook already exists and is verified.

nodes.label: B1 — Resource lifecycle / eviction
nodes.rationale: Caches (batchIds, bind-group/shader/pipeline, instancedPipelines) grow without eviction and destroy() is never called at teardown → leaks. Blocks refcounting in the asset system.

nodes.label: B2 — Editor ↔ nebula reconciliation
nodes.rationale: packages/editor targets a diverged nebula API that no longer compiles (RectNode, Node.position/scale, private Node.parent, missing Camera2D methods); partially unblocked by Camera2D.screenToWorld/worldToScreen.

nodes.label: B4 — 3D depth test
nodes.rationale: RenderState.depthTest / PassDescriptor.depth are inert yet already part of the pipeline cache keys — a silent trap; low priority while the engine is 2D-first.

nodes.label: Archetype / SoA storage backend
nodes.rationale: The swappable IComponentStore seam exists precisely to make this migration painless, but the implementation is still sparse-set only.

nodes.label: Changed<T> tick-based change detection
nodes.rationale: Bevy-style primitive intended to replace every residual manual diff; it is the hard dependency of B3 (killing the last Transform façade).

nodes.label: Scheduling Phase 3 — Physics dt
nodes.rationale: PhysicsWorld.step(dt) + world.timestep = dt is the single unfinished phase of the scheduling refactor.

nodes.label: C7 — Pixel-perfect smooth scroll
nodes.rationale: Render the world to a low-res render target at integer scale then upscale with a sub-pixel blit offset (Celeste technique) to get smoothness AND crispness, where pixelSnap alone advances the camera in 1px steps.

nodes.label: Camera2D.pixelSnap
nodes.rationale: Snaps the view matrix translation to the device grid 1/(zoom·dpr) to kill sub-pixel jitter and 1px tile seams, while keeping camera.position continuous so screenToWorld/follow are unaffected.

nodes.label: Named sorting layers + order-in-layer
nodes.rationale: Cross-cutting render feature touching SpriteRender, TileMapRenderer and NodeRendererBase.computeSortKey (free bits available) — to be designed separately, not as a tilemap feature.

nodes.label: Tilemap colliders
nodes.rationale: A component generating @atlasjs/rapier colliders from filled cells; depends on a gameplay-side 2D collision model.

nodes.label: Custom TypeScript compiler
nodes.rationale: One compiler serves both roadmaps: rewriting addComponent<T>(a,b) → addComponent(T,a,b), generating registerScriptMetadata, linking TProps ↔ metadata, and inlining token resolution to remove runtime dispatch.

nodes.label: B3 — Transform as pure data
nodes.rationale: Killing the last façade needs Changed<T>; the dragon is that teleporting a dynamic body cannot be a raw Transform write (clobbered next frame by the dynamic-only pull), so an explicit channel like rigidBody.teleport() is required.

nodes.label: Technical debt — dino-brawl tsc -b red
nodes.rationale: 4 pre-existing noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters errors in legacy non-ECS Player.ts and Sword.ts; unrelated to any design workstream.

nodes.label: Nexus ECS (@atlasjs/nexus)
nodes.rationale: Sparse-set ECS consumed by @atlasjs/gameplay; the refactor targeted one correctness bug already firing in prod, an entity-recycling time bomb, and a double indirection in the hot path.

nodes.label: Generational entities
nodes.rationale: Multiplicative index+generation packing (21-bit index) avoids BigInt on the hot path; stale handles now fail cleanly instead of silently applying to a recycled id (ABA).

nodes.label: IComponentStore seam
nodes.rationale: Makes a future SoA/archetype migration painless: systems never see this interface, they only see query, so the backend can be swapped without touching gameplay.

nodes.label: SparseSetStore
nodes.rationale: Sparse indexed by entityIndex (compact, bounded by peak live entities) while dense stores the full packed Entity, so dense[i] === entity also rejects stale handles.

nodes.label: Typed query with each()
nodes.rationale: The query already holds the stores, so handing components straight to the callback removes the per-entity requireComponent re-lookup and array allocation; args array is reused and applied, never spread.

nodes.label: Fail-fast structural-change guard
nodes.rationale: Version is checked BEFORE the bound test each iteration — otherwise a swap-remove shrinking size below the current index exits the loop before re-checking, silently skipping entities at counts of 1-2.

nodes.label: Hybrid command buffer
nodes.rationale: EnTT/flecs model: direct mutation by default, deferred via world.commands when mutating during a query. spawn() stays immediate because creating a bare entity touches no component store.

nodes.label: Auto-flush at lane Sync
nodes.rationale: NexusPlugin registers a nexus:flush step in the trailing Sync stage of all three lanes, so every plugin using the world gets flushing for free without wiring it.

nodes.label: ComponentRegistry
nodes.rationale: Replaces mutable module-global state and the ctor monkeypatch; a shared default registry keeps ids stable across worlds while injecting a fresh one gives total isolation for tests/hot-reload.

nodes.label: without / optional query filters
nodes.rationale: Immutable builder resolving extra stores through a StoreResolver so the query never depends on the concrete world; optional() does not affect membership, only widens the tuple with |undefined.

nodes.label: world.onAdd / world.onRemove
nodes.rationale: Mediated by the world rather than the store so IComponentStore stays unchanged; this is the brick that lets external entity-keyed storages (runtimeBodiesStorage) be cleaned automatically.

nodes.label: Structural mutation during iteration bug
nodes.rationale: Live-array iteration plus swap-remove made TransformWriteRequestCleanupSystem skip every other entity, so cleanup only partially drained each frame — the original motivation for the guard and the command buffer.

nodes.label: Perf target 1k–3k entities @ 60fps
nodes.rationale: At this scale pointer chasing and GC of class instances are negligible, so SoA/archetype would be engineering paid in DX with no visible gain; safety comes from the abstraction, not the representation.

nodes.label: Scheduling refactor
nodes.rationale: Two competing schedulers (core Scheduler + Nexus SystemScheduler) reconciled by hand in GameplayPlugin, plus 4 latent bugs meaning public contracts never ran; Nexus becomes a pure data store with ordering owned by one authority.

nodes.label: Named stage vocabulary (Stages.ts)
nodes.rationale: Numeric priorities overflowed their band without guardrails (gizmo 700+id), expressed no relation, and coupled every package to PRIORITY literals; a closed per-lane enum forces coarse ordering changes through reviewed vocabulary instead of magic numbers.

nodes.label: StepSpec (before / after constraints)
nodes.rationale: Fine ordering resolved by Kahn topo sort WITHIN a stage only (cross-stage edges are a clear error), with insertion order as stable tiebreak; pure before/after was rejected as under-constrained with unreadable errors.

nodes.label: StepHandle
nodes.rationale: onUpdate/onFixedUpdate/onRender returned void, so uninstall leaked steps (NebulaPlugin.unsubscribe always null, EditorPlugin could not remove picking/gizmo).

nodes.label: StepSet (groups)
nodes.rationale: Lets editor mode and scenes toggle whole groups at zero cost (steps stay registered, just disabled) and remove them wholesale at teardown.

nodes.label: StepContext (dt, alpha, tick, frame, elapsed)
nodes.rationale: A bare dt cannot carry alpha/tick, so every step signature had to change; the phase-0 compat façade deferred the chore and phase 8 assumed it.

nodes.label: Engine.advanceFixed seam
nodes.rationale: The single seam that keeps rollback netcode possible without building it today: a netcode driver would call advanceFixed with a per-tick input snapshot, outside RAF.

nodes.label: FrameClock
nodes.rationale: Monotonic tick/frame/elapsed/acc via performance.now; Date.now is banned in the fixed lane because the sim must be a pure function of (tick, fixedDelta, input snapshot).

nodes.label: Topological plugin boot (provides / requires)
nodes.rationale: Declares the DI contract already implicit in services.wait/provide; fixes the boot hang (a missing dep used to wait forever) via MissingDependencyError, DependencyCycleError, a boot timeout, and a post-install assertion.

nodes.label: Fixed-step determinism (rollback-ready, not deterministic)
nodes.rationale: Under the RAF driver (dt clamp 0.25 + maxSubSteps dropping time) the sim is NOT bit-exact across machines; the design is rollback-ready (advanceFixed seam + no wall-clock in sim), not deterministic today.

nodes.label: registerSystem adapter
nodes.rationale: Narrows StepContext to {world, dt} so gameplay systems register as ordinary scheduler steps, replacing the deleted SystemScheduler and the monolithic update().

nodes.label: SceneContext.scheduler (scene-scoped StepSet)
nodes.rationale: Makes scenes first-class schedulable citizens with no special case: SceneManager creates one set per active scene, auto-removed on destroy().

nodes.label: Engine loop: fixed×N → update → render+alpha
nodes.rationale: Running fixed before update changes feel (variable logic sees post-sim state in the same frame) but marries the interpolated render; scene.update became a registered step so there is no second inline entry point.

nodes.label: Dino Brawl cleanup workstream
nodes.rationale: Structural refactor preparing the app for gameplay scalability; explicitly excludes prefab/factory, data-driven Tiled spawns, and combat systems.

nodes.label: A script is per-frame behaviour; composition lives in the spawn function
nodes.rationale: The single guiding principle everything else derives from: PlayerScript.onCreate doing setScale/sortingOrder and WallScript.onCreate calling addComponent were static setup disguised as behaviour.
nodes.norm_label: a script is per-frame behaviour; composition lives in the spawn function

nodes.label: game/config.ts (SortingLayer, CollisionLayers, SortingOrder, MAP_SCALE)
nodes.rationale: Centralizes magic strings/numbers scattered across 4 files (shadow -1, shadow 8, player 10, wall 10, sword 20) so sort order is readable at a glance and collision layers are ready for the collisions workstream.

nodes.label: game/controls.ts (dinoControls + DinoControls)
nodes.rationale: defineActions and the Inputs type were duplicated across the scene and two scripts; the dead `hello` action (Key.MouseLeft, never read) is deleted.

nodes.label: game/spawn/* local spawn functions
nodes.rationale: Plain TS functions with no registry, no engine API and no generic abstraction — deliberately local because absorbing them is the job of the future prefab workstream; they also make multi-player parameterisable.

nodes.label: ArenaScene (ex EcsScene)
nodes.rationale: Renamed because EcsScene named the technology, not the role; reduced to defining sorting layers, loading the map, calling spawn* in order and activating the camera.

nodes.label: game/tiled/ in-place cleanup
nodes.rationale: Real defects fixed rather than extracted to a package: unassigned TileSet.tileWidth/tileHeight (type must tell the truth), the two compensating -1 offsets on firstGid/getId, missing return type on getSerializedLayer, the tileidth typo, and dead LayerManager.addLayer / TileLayer.

nodes.label: Dead code removal
nodes.rationale: WallScript, TileLayer, Window.tsx, the hello action, SwordScript.sprite, LayerManager.addLayer; also renames blueDinoSprite/blueDinoTexture which actually load the YELLOW dino.

nodes.label: app/ shell split (App / GameCanvas / DebugOverlay)
nodes.rationale: App.tsx mixed three concerns — React mounting, engine bootstrap (8 plugins, renderer, physics world, lifecycle) and the FPS debug overlay.

nodes.label: Zero behaviour change constraint
nodes.rationale: The game must stay strictly identical on screen, so verification is a visual before/after diff rather than a test suite; this is a structural refactor, not a gameplay evolution.

nodes.label: Dino Brawl cleanup implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Task-by-task checkbox plan (rename app → config/controls → React shell → tiled/ → dead code → spawn extraction) with build, lint, browser verify and a commit gate per task.

nodes.label: Browser verification protocol
nodes.rationale: The WebGPU pane serves stale scenes under HMR, so the dev server must be restarted rather than hot-reloaded; every visual task compares against a reference screenshot taken before task 1.

nodes.label: TileSet characterization test
nodes.rationale: Written to fail first, it pins getId arithmetic as numerically identical for every valid gid while fixing the off-by-one in isIdIn bounds; a differing tile in the browser is a stop-and-report gate, never something to mask.

nodes.label: firstGid normalization
nodes.rationale: The old code stored firstGid-1 then subtracted 1 again in getId; the two offsets cancelled, so normalizing to the real Tiled 1-based firstgid is byte-identical while eliminating the double -1. The y = columns-1-floor(...) line was deliberately preserved, not 'fixed'.

nodes.label: import type constraint under Vite
nodes.rationale: With verbatimModuleSyntax, a value import of a type-only symbol compiles under tsc but breaks Vite at runtime (black screen) — which is why browser verification is mandatory, not just a green build.

nodes.label: Tiled → Atlas bridge
nodes.rationale: Data-driven redesign of the existing app-local proto: takes a Tiled .tmj export and builds the scene from existing gameplay bricks; prerequisite for the tilemap-collision feature.

nodes.label: TiledDocument (pure parse layer)
nodes.rationale: Knows nothing of ECS, assets or Vite — pure parsing, unit-testable without a GPU; absorbs the old MapLoader/LayerManager/TileSetManager/MapObjectManager/MapObjectBuilder.

nodes.label: MapBuilder (ECS instantiation layer)
nodes.rationale: Orchestrates the ECS side (Grid + TileMap children + sprite entities) while staying policy-free: asset URL resolution and sorting policy are injected by the app.

nodes.label: resolveGid — flip-flag masking
nodes.rationale: The top 3 bits of a Tiled gid encode H/V/diagonal flips and make the number look negative, so the raw value must go through >>> 0 before masking; diagonal flip is masked but not applied in v1.

nodes.label: Tiled↔Atlas row-flip
nodes.rationale: Tiled numbers tiles top→bottom (local id 0 = top-left) while Atlas addresses them bottom→top, so localIndex = (rows-1-tiledRow)*columns+col with rows = tileCount/columns. The proto used columns as the base, which is only correct for square tilesets.

nodes.label: TiledAssetResolver (import.meta.glob)
nodes.rationale: The JSON `image` field is a runtime string, not a module, so Vite never rewrites it to the bundled hashed URL → 404 in prod. Matching is on `image` (tied to the file on disk), not `name` (an editable display label).

nodes.label: groupNameSortingResolver
nodes.rationale: Convention over configuration: walk groupPath inside-out and take the first case-insensitive match against the declared sorting layers, with an explicit override map and a warned fallback.

nodes.label: BuiltMap result
nodes.rationale: Returns grid, tile-layer entities, object entities, collider data and named points already in WORLD coordinates, so ArenaScene no longer multiplies the spawn point by MAP_SCALE.

nodes.label: Data-only collision decision
nodes.rationale: No Collider2D/RigidBody2D is spawned by the bridge; shapes are only exposed so the following tilemap-collision feature owns that decision, keeping this task's scope closed.

nodes.label: Tile-objects as Y-sorted entities
nodes.rationale: Y-sort is per-entity, not per-tile: a whole TileMap shares one worldY, so anything that must interleave with the player (occluders like trees) MUST be a tile-object, never a tile layer. Sprites are anchored at their base so worldY is the feet.

nodes.label: Multi-tileset layer split
nodes.rationale: One Tiled layer becomes N TileMap children (one per tileset used), replacing the proto's fragile '1 Tiled tileset = 1 gameplay layer matched by name' assumption; yields one instanced draw call per (layer × tileset).

nodes.label: Parse/ECS boundary principle
nodes.rationale: Keeping the Vite and policy pieces as injected seams is exactly what would later allow extracting the bridge into an @atlasjs/tiled engine package without dragging import.meta.glob along.

nodes.label: Tiled bridge implementation plan
nodes.rationale: TDD task plan (gid → TiledDocument → resolver → sorting → map math → MapBuilder → migration), app-local only, with the user reviewing and committing each task.

nodes.label: Post-implementation row-flip correction
nodes.rationale: The plan originally asserted Tiled local index == Atlas linear index with no flip; browser verification proved this false, so the plan's Task 2 / Task 5 localIndex assertions are marked obsolete in favour of the committed code and the corrected spec.

nodes.label: Isolated raw Tiled JSON types
nodes.rationale: tiled.raw.types.ts is kept separate from the legacy tiled.types.ts so every intermediate commit stays green until the legacy files are deleted together with their consumers in the final task.

nodes.label: Camera component (LEVEL 1)
nodes.rationale: Pure data (just zoom) with no LEVEL 2 façade, because there is nothing to route — activation goes through the service, not the component (the 'no façade by symmetry' invariant, precedent PlayerInput).

nodes.label: CameraManager (CAMERA_MANAGER)
nodes.rationale: Single authority over the active camera and screen↔world; deliberately the seam where multi-camera would later grow (setActive → add/setLayer, screenToWorld(entity?)).

nodes.label: CameraSyncSystem
nodes.rationale: Runs in render/PreRender before sprite-render (whose culling reads getCameraViewport) and in strict order zoom → read viewport → position, since the viewport extent depends on the current zoom. It resolves the single active entity rather than iterating a query.

nodes.label: CameraApi script service façade
nodes.rationale: Exact mirror of InputApi (ScriptService<CameraManager>, static token) so scripts get screenToWorld/worldToScreen/setMain without nebula ever leaking.

nodes.label: Camera2D.screenToWorld / worldToScreen
nodes.rationale: Placed on Camera2D because it owns the matrix and the editor can reuse it; analytic (no Mat4.invert) because without camera rotation the ortho (0,w,h,0) and the mouse space cancel out. Takes an optional out to avoid allocations.

nodes.label: Centering baked into the view matrix
nodes.rationale: nebula stays top-left ('just a matrix') while the Unity-like centered convention lives entirely in gameplay: once renderer.camera.position = center − viewport/2, screenToWorld stays the simple top-left formula and automatically honours centering — only the sync needs to know the viewport size.
nodes.norm_label: centering baked into the view matrix

nodes.label: Single active camera
nodes.rationale: Many camera entities may exist but only one drives rendering, keeping nebula's one-pass model untouched; the gameplay camera is just another producer writing into renderer.camera, like the editor in edit mode.

nodes.label: Follow via parenting
nodes.rationale: Because the sync reads WorldTransform2D (world, not local position), making the camera a child of the player gives follow behaviour for free with no dedicated system.

nodes.label: Two hierarchies, two responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Nexus owns structure (transform-agnostic), gameplay owns transform composition, and the render bridge keeps nebula nodes flat — the Bevy split. Routing entity structure through the nebula SceneGraph would make the editor and physics depend on the renderer.

nodes.label: Parent component
nodes.rationale: The relation is stored as data (hence queryable and serializable); Parent is carried by the child and roots are found with query(...).without(Parent).

nodes.label: Children component
nodes.rationale: API-maintained and read-only outside; getChildren returns the LIVE array (not a defensive copy) typed ReadonlyArray, so it must not be mutated nor retained across setParent/destroyEntity.

nodes.label: world.setParent / getParent / getChildren
nodes.rationale: Updates both sides atomically, throws on cycles, is idempotent, and destroys descendants recursively by default (Unity style); reparenting inside a query().each() is structural and must go through world.commands.setParent.

nodes.label: Mat3 completion (multiply / invert / decompose)
nodes.rationale: Makes Mat3 a full 2D affine matrix (useful for physics, rendering and editor gizmos) and avoids dragging Mat4's 16 floats where 9 suffice; matrix composition is exact under shear where naive TRS composition is approximate. invert is what powers worldPositionStays.

nodes.label: WorldTransform2D
nodes.rationale: Transform2D becomes the LOCAL transform (backwards compatible while everything is a root) and WorldTransform2D carries the derived world matrix, created and removed automatically by propagation.

nodes.label: TransformPropagationSystem
nodes.rationale: Walks roots→leaves so a parent is always computed before its children; a dynamic body ignores parent composition (physics is authority) but its children still compose on its world. V1 recomputes the whole tree each frame.

nodes.label: worldPositionStays reparent semantics
nodes.rationale: Defaults to true like Unity: local = parentWorld.invert() * currentWorld is recomputed so the world pose does not move; with false the local is reinterpreted in the new frame and the child snaps.

nodes.label: Lossy TRS decomposition at the render edge
nodes.rationale: The flat SpriteNode consumes TRS, not a matrix, so the world matrix is decomposed — exact everywhere except a sheared quad (non-uniform parent scale + nested rotation), the same tradeoff as Unity's lossyScale. Physics is rigid so it is always exact.
nodes.norm_label: lossy trs decomposition at the render edge

nodes.label: One-frame physics latency
nodes.rationale: Propagation sits at the end of the update lane, so render reads a fresh world transform the same frame while fixed/PhysicsRequest reads last frame's — exactly the latency physics already tolerates. Pure visual children (health bars, weapons, decor) are 100% exact.

nodes.label: PhysicsPull restricted to dynamic bodies
nodes.rationale: Writing body world into Transform2D for every body would overwrite a kinematic/static child's LOCAL transform with WORLD data — silent corruption; restricting the pull to dynamic is also what the declared authority model demands.

nodes.label: registerScriptMetadata registry
nodes.rationale: A plain-JS WeakMap keyed by constructor replaced the stage-3 @Expose decorator: no shared Symbol between writer and reader, no leak when a class is unloaded, and inheritance is merged at read time (child overrides parent per field) so a base class is never polluted.

nodes.label: ScriptMetadata.field() / .entity() builders
nodes.rationale: Namespaced by declaration merging (interface + const of the same name, no `namespace` keyword), in the same spirit as button()/vector2() on the input side; they always set the discriminant.

nodes.label: ExposeFieldMetadata discriminated union
nodes.rationale: Stores only what the runtime needs (discriminant + required?) and stays open to extension so the compiler/editor can add kind/assetKind/runtimeType/tooltip later — no speculative editor schema is frozen now.

nodes.label: GameEntity handle
nodes.rationale: Transposes Unity's GameObject reference: wraps (world, entity, resolver) statelessly, caching no component data and re-resolving each call, so a destroyed entity yields undefined rather than dangling data.

nodes.label: ScriptResolver interface
nodes.rationale: GameEntity lives in scripting/core and depends on this interface rather than the concrete runtime ScriptManager, preserving the runtime → core dependency direction and avoiding a cycle.

nodes.label: AttachProps mapped type
nodes.rationale: Lets a field be typed GameEntity inside the script but passed as a raw Entity at the attach call site; works because GameEntity is a method-rich interface no plain value matches, and Entity (number & brand) does not match GameEntity.

nodes.label: injectProps — warn, never throw
nodes.rationale: Only exposed fields are assigned; a missing required field or an unexposed key warns but never throws so the game does not break. Injection happens after construction and before onCreate, so scripts can read injected fields in onCreate.

nodes.label: AtlasScript<TProps> phantom typing
nodes.rationale: A declared-but-never-assigned __props field carries TProps purely for inference; the {} default keeps every existing prop-less script compiling unchanged.

nodes.label: The GPU boundary is correct, not a limitation
nodes.rationale: A script must never build a texture/sprite/animation — exactly Unity's model where you receive a reference via [SerializeField] instead of calling new Texture(). Composition root fabricates, game logic consumes; all four listed frictions share this single root cause.
nodes.norm_label: the gpu boundary is correct, not a limitation

nodes.label: Babel / decorator toolchain removal
nodes.rationale: @Expose required Babel in vitest and in every app plus a fragile top-level Symbol.metadata polyfill and clone-on-own-write inheritance handling; replacing it with an explicit registry removed the whole chain.

nodes.label: TProps ↔ metadata desync caveat
nodes.rationale: Every injectable field is declared twice — in the AtlasScript<{...}> generic and in registerScriptMetadata — with no automatic link, so a field renamed on one side stays silently undefined. Inherent until the custom compiler generates both.

nodes.label: GameEntity must be import type
nodes.rationale: A value import passes tsc --noEmit (erased at type-check) but breaks at runtime under Vite/esbuild with 'does not provide an export named GameEntity' → black screen; must be verified in the browser, not just by tsc.

nodes.label: getScript before onCreate caveat
nodes.rationale: getScript returns an instance as soon as it is registered, possibly before its onCreate ran; within one flush attach order equals flushCreates order, so read other scripts' state in onUpdate rather than onCreate.

nodes.label: Gameplay & scripting redesign
nodes.rationale: Net result: ~7 systems + 3 storages + 3 types collapse into 2 systems + 1 component + thin handles.

nodes.label: Shadow ECS (4 copies of one datum)
nodes.rationale: ScriptComponentStorage was a second ECS over Nexus: duplicate types, a duplicate vector type (Vector2D vs Vec2), and a diff/request/feedback machine whose only job was copying one into the other, with per-entity per-frame allocations in the hot path.
nodes.norm_label: shadow ecs (4 copies of one datum)

nodes.label: Unity C++↔C# split is a proxy, not a copy
nodes.rationale: Unity's C# Transform is a thin handle whose accessors cross interop and read/write the C++ memory directly — one source of truth, a window on it. That split exists because a hard technical frontier (managed/GC vs native) forces it; in TypeScript there is no such frontier, so the cost of separation was paid without the constraint that justifies it.
nodes.norm_label: unity c++↔c# split is a proxy, not a copy

nodes.label: Thin façade handle
nodes.rationale: A handle holds no data, only (world, entity), so `this.transform.position.x += 10` mutates the single source of truth — encapsulation kept, sync deleted. Façades are reserved for ENGINE components (authority/encapsulation); user data components like Health are accessed directly.

nodes.label: ScriptComponentRegistry (lazy resolve + event-invalidated cache)
nodes.rationale: Only a found instance is cached, never absence, so a later addComponent is seen on next access without listening to onAdd; onRemove invalidates. Re-resolving every access would already be negligible at target scale — the cache is an optimisation, not a requirement.

nodes.label: Contract: mutate in place, never replace
nodes.rationale: world.setComponent replaces the instance without emitting onRemove, the one operation that would silently stale the handle cache; the alternative is hardening Nexus to emit onRemove+onAdd on replacement.
nodes.norm_label: contract: mutate in place, never replace

nodes.label: PhysicsBodyRef component
nodes.rationale: Turning the inertia body handle into a normal Nexus component lets queries join it and lets onRemove destroy the body — deleting the hand-managed SparseSet and the manual plugin hook. Runtime-only, never serialized.

nodes.label: PhysicsPushSystem
nodes.rationale: Creates missing bodies (via world.commands since it iterates) and pushes velocity plus, for kinematic/static, position/rotation into the solver.

nodes.label: PhysicsPullSystem
nodes.rationale: Writes back only for dynamic bodies; reading kinematic back would recreate a second authority over the same datum.

nodes.label: Authority declared by body type
nodes.rationale: 'What if I move both at once' disappears: per entity exactly one authority owns position, decided at write time by reading RigidBody2D.type. Dynamic is moved by velocity/force and setPosition is an explicit teleport, never a silent clobber.

nodes.label: Vec2 everywhere (Vector2D deleted)
nodes.rationale: Vector2D existed only to serve the shadow layer and was copied field by field into Vec2; removing the shadow layer removed the need for it.

nodes.label: Dynamic teleport before body creation
nodes.rationale: On the first frame PhysicsBodyRef may not exist yet, so setPosition must fall back to writing Transform2D (used as the initial translation at body creation) instead of calling a non-existent body.

nodes.label: ScriptService<TService> façade base
nodes.rationale: Symmetric to ScriptComponent (static engine) with a static token resolved through the engine's ServiceRegistry — no global static, so multi-engine and testable; throws loudly at construction if the token or service is missing.

nodes.label: Service cached at constructor (divergence from ScriptComponent)
nodes.rationale: A service is never un-provided (ServiceRegistry has no unprovide) so the reference cannot go stale — unlike a component, whose membership is mutable and forces re-resolution. This divergence is intentional and must not be 'aligned' with ScriptComponent.
nodes.norm_label: service cached at constructor (divergence from scriptcomponent)

nodes.label: InputApi curated façade
nodes.rationale: Named distinctly from the backend Input interface; exposes only read-only polling (isDown/isPressed/isReleased, mousePosition/mouseDelta/scrollDelta) and never lets endFrame/clearAll/keys/pointer reach a script.

nodes.label: defineActions + button()/value()/vector2() builders
nodes.rationale: Authoring produces a serializable data descriptor (not runtime objects) and lifts the name→kind map into the type system, so map.get("jump") is typed and a wrong name is a compile error — aligned with the engine's serialization/editor direction.

nodes.label: InputActionMap runtime
nodes.rationale: Each action keeps current + previous so edges are correct at the ACTION level, not just the key level; that transition point is the seam where events and interactions will plug in.

nodes.label: Vector2Action
nodes.rationale: Raw composite in v1: a WASD diagonal returns (1,1), not (0.707,0.707); normalisation is deferred to an optional processor.

nodes.label: PlayerInput component
nodes.rationale: A raw Nexus component with no façade: there is no authority to route, and the action handles already ARE the curated read API — adding a third concept would be pure ceremony.

nodes.label: PlayerInputSystem
nodes.rationale: Samples at update/Early — after the DOM backend filled the frame, before scripts at Logic, and before endFrame clears edges at Late. Resolves INPUT lazily so gameplay does not declare it in requires and there is no boot coupling.

nodes.label: isDown / isPressed / isReleased vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Backend naming is kept across all three layers (backend, InputApi, actions) rather than adopting Unity's getKey*; introducing wasPressedThisFrame or redefining isPressed as held is explicitly forbidden.

nodes.label: Persistent action handles mutated in place
nodes.rationale: Action objects live in the map and are mutated each frame, so a reference grabbed once in onCreate stays valid for the entity's lifetime — never re-created per frame or per get().
nodes.norm_label: persistent action handles mutated in place

nodes.label: dt threaded through sample()
nodes.rationale: Unused in v1 but passed anyway so time-based interactions (hold/tap) can be added later without changing the signature; it must not be removed 'because it is unused'.

nodes.label: Read input in onUpdate, not onFixedUpdate
nodes.rationale: Edges are per update-frame and valid at stage Logic (before endFrame at Late); in the fixed lane, which runs 0..N times per frame, they are ambiguous. Documented, with no runtime guard.
nodes.norm_label: read input in onupdate, not onfixedupdate

nodes.label: Live mutable Vec2 returned to scripts
nodes.rationale: mousePosition/mouseDelta and Vector2Action.readValue() hand back the live backend Vec2, which a script could mutate; cloning would allocate on every access every frame, so it was rejected and the risk is watched instead.
nodes.norm_label: live mutable vec2 returned to scripts
